updates.title: AWS Lambda exports durable-run telemetry and adds an MCP query server
updates.whatChanged: AWS released the open-source Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter and a companion MCP server on 28 October. The exporter records each durable run's status, steps, waits, retries, timing, input and output, then sends a JSON record to one or more of 13 destinations. The MCP server queries TypeScript, Python and Java records read-only.
updates.whyCare: You can query a durable workflow across Lambda invocations without joining invocation logs and traces by hand. An MCP client can inspect records without writing queries for each data store.
updates.before: Lambda stored logs per invocation, splitting a durable run across streams. Teams had to aggregate records to analyze failures across runs.
updates.after: The exporter emits one structured record per execution and routes it to selected stores. An MCP server lets agents query supported records read-only.
updates.learn: Choose a destination and retention plan for run records. Redact inputs and outputs before export. Give the MCP server read-only AWS credentials.

updates.architectureImplication: Treat run telemetry as a separate data product. Route records to stores that match your retention and query needs. Scope MCP access to read-only credentials.
